corpus_gaps: Partition Law No. 21 of 1977 is not in the corpus. It is the enactment that governs both the partition action and the statutory conditions on a deed of partition between co-owners, and it is the central authority for advising three co-owners of a single 30-perch land who want separate divided lots. Apartment Ownership Law s.23 refers to 'the Partition Law' but the corpus holds no text of it.

The Roman-Dutch common law of usufruct and life interest is not statutory and is absent. Whether the three sons, as holders of the bare dominium subject to their father's reserved life interest, may sell, mortgage or build during the father's lifetime, and what a deed of renunciation or release of a life interest achieves, cannot be answered from the corpus.
The Roman-Dutch common law of co-ownership (rights of a co-owner to alienate an undivided share, to build on the common land, and the improvements/compensation rules) is not statutory and is absent.

Subdivision and minimum-lot control for Battaramulla is not in the corpus: no Urban Development Authority subdivision regulations, no Sri Jayewardenepura Kotte municipal building or blocking-out rules, and no rates schedule. Whether 30 perches can lawfully be split into three divided lots therefore cannot be resolved here.

Stamp duty and notarial fee rate schedules for a deed of partition, a deed of transfer of an undivided share, or a deed of release of a life interest are not extracted, so no figure can be given for the cost of any of the routes considered.

Case law is out of scope for this corpus by design; the question asks for the 'most appropriate' conveyancing route, which in Sri Lankan practice is settled by judicial authority on co-ownership and life interests as much as by statute.

provisions.formal_title: Prevention of Frauds Ordinance No. 7 of 1840
provisions.relevant_excerpt: No sale, purchase, transfer, assignment, or mortgage of land or other immovable property, and no promise, bargain, contract, or agreement for effecting any such object, or for establishing any security, interest, or incumbrance affecting land or other immovable property (other than a lease at will, or for any period not exceeding one month)
provisions.why_relevant: Every instrument any of the three brothers would need — a deed of transfer of Asanka's undivided share, a deed of partition between the three, a deed of release of the father's life interest, or the mortgage bond Sasanka must give for a housing loan — is a transfer or a security affecting immovable property, so it has no force in law unless it is executed and attested before a notary in the manner this section prescribes. It fixes the form of whatever route is advised, not the choice between routes.
provisions.temporal_note: In force since 1840; the notarial-execution requirement for transfers, mortgages and agreements affecting land was in force at 2018-10. The corpus body is the consolidated text carrying amendments by Act No. 30 of 2022 s.2 and Act No. 4 of 2024 s.2, both after the matter date; the excerpt taken is the opening words of subsection (1), which the 2022 and 2024 amendments did not introduce. The detail of paragraphs (a) and (b) (thumb impressions, transferee signature) reflects the post-2022 text and must not be applied to a 2018 matter.

provisions.formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
provisions.relevant_excerpt: all instruments, including wills, decrees and orders of any court or authority, and awards, which purport or operate to create, confer, declare, limit, assign, transfer, charge, incumber, release, or extinguish any right, title, or interest, whether vested or contingent, past, present, or future, to, in or over land
provisions.why_relevant: Brings each of the candidate instruments within the registration Chapter: a deed of partition limits and assigns interests in the land, a deed of release extinguishes the father's life interest, a transfer of Asanka's share assigns it, and a mortgage bond incumbers it. Without this section, s.7's priority rule has nothing to bite on.
provisions.temporal_note: In force since 1927 with no recorded change year in the corpus; applicable at 2018-10.

provisions.formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
provisions.relevant_excerpt: be void as against all parties claiming an adverse interest thereto on valuable consideration by virtue of any subsequent instrument which is duly registered under this Chapter
provisions.why_relevant: Whatever route the brothers take, the resulting deed must be registered in the land registry of the district, or it will lose priority to a later registered instrument taken for value. This is why the practical advice ends with registration, and it is what makes Sasanka's lender willing to accept the security.
provisions.temporal_note: In force since 1927 with no recorded change year in the corpus; applicable at 2018-10.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: The Law shall apply to any building- (a) erected on alienated land held as one Sand parcel and capable of being subdivided into parcels (hereinafter referred to as "Condominium Property")
provisions.why_relevant: Asanka's stated wish is to buy an apartment in Colombo. This section identifies when the Apartment Ownership Law governs the building he would be buying into, and so which statutory regime, rather than ordinary land law, describes what he acquires.
provisions.temporal_note: In force since 1973; last amended in the corpus by Act No. 39 of 2003 s.3, before the matter date. Applicable at 2018-10.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: after the registration of a Condominium Plan, or Semi Condominium Plan, any condominium parcel depicted therein together with the common elements appurtenant thereto may be held and dealt with in the same manner and form as any land.
provisions.why_relevant: Explains what Asanka would get for the proceeds of his share: a condominium parcel that can be owned, sold and mortgaged like land, rather than a further undivided share. It is the statutory answer to the apartment limb of the advice.
provisions.temporal_note: In force since 1973; subsection (4) as it stands reflects amendment by Act No. 39 of 2003 s.13, before the matter date. Applicable at 2018-10.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: No share in the common elements of a registered, Condominium Property or of a registered Semi Condominium Property shall be disposed of or otherwise dealt with except as appurtenant to a condominium parcel of such property
provisions.why_relevant: Qualifies the ownership Asanka would acquire: his share of the common elements is tied to the parcel and cannot be dealt with separately. Relevant to advising him on the difference between the co-ownership he is leaving and the apartment ownership he is entering.
provisions.temporal_note: In force since 1973; the text in the corpus reflects replacement by Act No. 39 of 2003 s.16, before the matter date. Applicable at 2018-10.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: No person acquiring an title or interest or benefit in any condominium parcel of a registered Condominium Property or of a registered Semi Condominium Property shall be entitled to such title or interest, or benefit, unless such title, or interest or benefit is registered under the provisions of Registration of Title Act. No. 21 of 1998.
provisions.why_relevant: Sets the registration step Asanka must take on the apartment purchase, and shows that the apartment side of the advice runs under the Registration of Title Act rather than the deeds registration Chapter that governs the Battaramulla land.
provisions.temporal_note: In force since 1973; the present text was substituted by Act No. 39 of 2003 s.15, before the matter date. Applicable at 2018-10.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: includes things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything attached to the earth, and any estate, right, or interest in or over land
provisions.why_relevant: Context for Sasanka's housing loan: for mortgage purposes 'land' extends to any estate, right or interest in or over land, so an interest short of full divided ownership is capable of being mortgaged. It does not by itself tell us whether a lender would accept his interest, and it is recorded as background only.
provisions.temporal_note: In force since 1949 with no recorded change year in the corpus; applicable at 2018-10. Note that the corpus text of this interpretation section has lost the defined terms themselves, so the excerpt reads as a bare 'includes' clause; the verifier should confirm from the source that it is the definition of 'land'.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: The Partition Law shall not apply to any land or building comprised in any registered Condominium Plan.
provisions.why_relevant: Recorded as background because it is the only place in the corpus that acknowledges the Partition Law, which is the enactment the answer to this question actually turns on and which the corpus does not contain. It also marks the boundary between the two regimes in play: the Battaramulla land and the Colombo apartment.
provisions.temporal_note: In force since 1973 with no recorded change year in the corpus; applicable at 2018-10.

questions.authority_requirement_reason: The question asks for the most appropriate conveyancing route for three brothers who hold a single 30-perch Battaramulla land in undivided shares under a deed of gift that reserves their father's life interest. Deciding that route requires (i) the Roman-Dutch common law of usufruct, to say what the sons can and cannot do while their father's life interest subsists and what a deed of renunciation would achieve, (ii) the Roman-Dutch common law of co-ownership, to say whether a co-owner may sell an undivided share, build on the common land or claim for improvements, and (iii) the Partition Law No. 21 of 1977, for both an amicable deed of partition and a partition action. None of the three is in the corpus. The statutes that are in the corpus govern only the form of the instruments (notarial execution, registration) and the apartment Asanka wants to buy, which is downstream of the choice the question asks about.

legal_issues.issue: What rights the three sons hold under a deed of gift subject to the donor's reserved life interest, and whether they may sell, mortgage or build on the land while their father is alive.
Whether Asanka may sell his undivided one-third share to a stranger, and what a purchaser of an undivided share subject to a life interest would in practice acquire.

Whether the three brothers can convert their undivided shares into divided lots, by a deed of partition or otherwise, and whether a 30-perch land carrying one house can lawfully be divided three ways.
What a lender needs before it will grant Sasanka a housing loan on the security of his interest, and what instrument must be executed.
What Asanka acquires if he applies the proceeds to buying an apartment in Colombo, and how that title is created and registered.
The form and registration requirements common to every instrument the advice would produce.

questions.hop_count_basis: No indispensable statutory chain can be fixed while the governing authority (Partition Law No. 21 of 1977, Roman-Dutch usufruct and co-ownership) is outside the corpus. The provisions recorded here support the form and the apartment limb of the advice, not the choice of route, so no indispensable dependency is asserted and the hop count is left at 0.

enrichment.original_background: Upali de Silva executed a Deed of Gift subject to his Life Interest gifting his property situated in Battaramulla in extent of 30 perches with a house standing thereon to his 3 sons Asanka, Sasanka and Kanishka. Asanka wishes to sell his share and purchase an Apartment in Colombo. Sasanka wishes to obtain a housing loan and build a house on his share. Kanishka wishes to live in the house built on the land.

gold_answer_draft.issue: Three brothers hold a single 30-perch Battaramulla land, with one house on it, in undivided shares under a deed of gift that reserved their father's life interest. One wants to sell out and buy a Colombo apartment, one wants a housing loan and a house of his own on the land, and one wants to live in the existing house. The issue is which conveyancing route best gives each of them what he wants, and what each brother can lawfully do while the life interest subsists. This draft is incomplete: the authority that decides the route is outside the corpus and the answer is reserved.
gold_answer_draft.rule: Two things can be stated from the corpus. First, whichever route is chosen, the instrument that carries it must take notarial form and be registered. Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2 provides that no sale, purchase, transfer, assignment or mortgage of land, and no agreement for effecting any such object or for establishing any security or incumbrance affecting land, is in force or avails in law unless executed and attested in the manner prescribed; Registration of Documents Ordinance s.8(b) brings within the registration Chapter every instrument that creates, limits, assigns, transfers, incumbers, releases or extinguishes any interest in land, which covers a transfer of an undivided share, a deed of partition, a release of a life interest and a mortgage bond alike; and s.7(1) makes an unregistered instrument void against a later instrument taken for value and duly registered. Second, on the apartment Asanka wants to buy, Apartment Ownership Law s.2(a) applies that Law to a building erected on alienated land held as one land parcel and capable of subdivision into parcels; s.9(4) provides that after registration of the condominium plan a condominium parcel with its appurtenant common elements may be held and dealt with in the same manner and form as any land; s.11 ties the share in the common elements to the parcel, so it cannot be dealt with separately; and s.10(1) requires the title to be registered under the Registration of Title Act before the purchaser is entitled to it. What the corpus does not supply is the rule that decides the question actually asked: the effect of the reserved life interest on the sons' powers of alienation, building and mortgage; the rights of a co-owner of an undivided share; and the Partition Law No. 21 of 1977, which governs both an amicable deed of partition and a partition action. Apartment Ownership Law s.23 refers to that Partition Law but the corpus holds none of its text.
gold_answer_draft.application: Asanka can be told what he would be buying if he does acquire a Colombo apartment: a condominium parcel that, once the plan is registered, is dealt with like land, carrying an inseparable share of the common elements, and vesting in him only on registration under the Registration of Title Act. All three can be told that any deed they execute over the Battaramulla land must be notarially attested and promptly registered, and that a deed left unregistered will lose to a later registered deed for value, which is the point their lender will care about. Beyond that the advice cannot be completed on the corpus. Whether Asanka can sell an undivided one-third that is burdened by his father's life interest, and whether a purchaser would take anything of present value, turns on the law of usufruct. Whether Sasanka can build on a specific part of a commonly owned 30 perches before division, and whether a bank would take a mortgage of a bare undivided share subject to a life interest, turns on the law of co-ownership and on lending practice, not on any provision in the corpus; the Mortgage Act interpretation section shows only that an estate, right or interest in or over land is capable of being mortgaged. Whether the obvious practical route, a release of the father's life interest followed by a partition among the three, is available depends on the Partition Law, and whether 30 perches with one house can be split into three lots depends on Urban Development Authority and local authority subdivision rules for Battaramulla. None of that is in the corpus, and the extent of the land makes the point live rather than academic.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The question is reserved as blocked for missing authority. A complete answer requires the Partition Law No. 21 of 1977, the Roman-Dutch law of usufruct and co-ownership, and the subdivision controls applying to Battaramulla, none of which the corpus contains. What can be stated on the corpus, and only as far as it goes, is that any instrument the brothers execute over the land must be notarially attested under Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2 and registered under Registration of Documents Ordinance ss.7 and 8 to hold its priority, and that an apartment bought by Asanka would give him a condominium parcel dealt with as land under Apartment Ownership Law s.9(4), with an inseparable share of the common elements under s.11, effective on registration under s.10(1).

answer_claims.claim_text: Any transfer of an undivided share, deed of partition, release of a life interest or mortgage bond over the Battaramulla land is a transfer of, or a security affecting, immovable property and has no force in law unless executed and attested in the notarial manner prescribed by the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance.

Each of those instruments is an instrument affecting land for the purposes of the Registration of Documents Ordinance, because each creates, limits, assigns, transfers, incumbers, releases or extinguishes an interest in land.

An instrument affecting the land that is not duly registered is void against a party claiming an adverse interest for valuable consideration under a later instrument that is duly registered, so registration is a necessary step whichever route the brothers take.

The Apartment Ownership Law applies to a building erected on alienated land held as one land parcel and capable of being subdivided into parcels, which is the regime that would govern an apartment bought in Colombo.

Once the condominium plan is registered, a condominium parcel together with its appurtenant common elements may be held and dealt with in the same manner and form as any land, and the share in the common elements cannot be disposed of except as appurtenant to the parcel.

A purchaser of a condominium parcel is not entitled to the title, interest or benefit acquired unless it is registered under the Registration of Title Act, so the apartment purchase is completed by registration under that Act rather than under the deeds registration Chapter that governs the Battaramulla land.

If Asanka sells out and buys an apartment in Colombo, what he acquires is a condominium parcel dealt with as land, carrying a share in the common elements that is inseparable from the parcel, and vesting in him on registration.

For mortgage purposes an estate, right or interest in or over land is itself capable of being mortgaged, but this does not establish that a lender would advance a housing loan against Sasanka's undivided share while his father's life interest subsists.

The choice of the most appropriate route cannot be settled on this corpus, because the Partition Law No. 21 of 1977, the law of usufruct governing the reserved life interest and the law of co-ownership governing undivided shares are all outside it, and the Apartment Ownership Law refers to the Partition Law without supplying its text.

What can be advised on the corpus is confined to form and registration for the Battaramulla land and to the nature of the title on the Colombo apartment; the question is therefore reserved for the missing authority.

questions.block_reason: The decisive authority is not in the frozen corpus. Advising on the most appropriate route for three co-owners of a 30-perch Battaramulla land held subject to their donor father's reserved life interest requires the Partition Law No. 21 of 1977 (absent), the Roman-Dutch common law of usufruct and of co-ownership (non-statutory, absent), and the Urban Development Authority and local authority subdivision controls for Battaramulla (absent). The corpus supports only the form and registration of the instruments and the apartment-ownership limb, so no indispensable statutory chain can be asserted and the question cannot be proposed as statute-only gold.
